commits.message:
Effected lights a Loop on the colours it draws (rich-effects-cbgp.071) (#392)

* Effected measures what its child draws; onColors and wheel read it (rich-effects-cbgp.071)

An effect is now handed what the element draws in the frame (`Drawn`: the
ink/ground pairs of its word cells, its own colours and fills, the depth and
theme), measured in Effected's render off the same per-segment reading its
cells are drawn from. `onColors(loop, colors?)` settles its shares against
that measurement, memoized per set of colours drawn; `wheel(curve, z)` reads
its colours and fills from it. `drawnOf` exposes the same measurement.

Strip and FlexStrip stamp every join they draw with the `JOIN` owner, so a
seam is left out of the words kept legible without the caller's help.

The effects-feel demo's copy of that measurement (drawnSubject's pairs and
colours, subjectUnder, fills, cellsOf, shown, seamed) is gone; its frames are
byte-identical across 4 themes x 3 depths x 4 loops x 10 instants.

`shares` leaves the barrel: no caller needs it now.

* A lit colour no word cell shows takes the whole touch, not a throw mid-render (rich-effects-cbgp.071)

shares refused a colour written in no pair. That was a caller's mistake when
the caller passed the pairs; now Effected measures them each frame, and a
frame drawing a lit fill only under blanks, or not at all, threw from render.
Whole-keys settle reads a chunk's rest in full when a sink throws mid-drain (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Whole-keys settle: ESC [ / ESC O is the Alt chord; settling survives a throwing sink (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Review fixes: whole-keys feed no longer runs the split hold logic; header
names InputChunks; docs Input field typed; integration test that a
NodeTerminalHost in the docs worker reads whole-keys. Split-host residue
filed as rich-host-input-gnl7.

A whole-keys host settles each input chunk; no lone ESC is held for a timer (rich-host-input-ab9n)

TerminalHost declares inputChunks: xterm.js (BrowserTerminalHost, and the
docs worker's simulated stdin through NodeTerminalHost) never splits a key
across chunks, so an ESC left at a chunk's end is Escape and what followed
it is re-read. A tty stays "split" and keeps the setTimeout(0) hold.
